Staff ripped me off then insulted me
Nov 2019 • Family
This review is to serve as a warning to other visitors and to bring this to the attention of the restaurant management. I was at the restaurant just a couple of hours ago as part of a full day Ho Chi Minh City tour with TNK travels. We were there for lunch. The restaurant looks lovely with lots of greenery and a pool in the middle. The food was alright and service was quick, however, it was at the end of service that the problem happened. Drinks were not included in our tour package so we ordered them separately, mum and I ordered a passion fruit juice and a lime juice. I paid the bill and noticed that I was short of some change when the staff returned with my change. When I asked him about it, he said something on his language to another staff member who pulled some change out of her own wallet and gave it to me. It was a little more than what I was owed but before I could say anything, the first staff member, Tony, turned to me and said ‘ you can keep the extra as a tip’. Which was obviously an insult. First of all, some of you may already know that Vietnamese currency is complicated, they have no coins, only notes and they even have notes for 500,000 Dong. So when I was short changed, while I really didn’t care whether a paltry 800 dong was given to me or not, I was more curious about whether they actually even have notes for small amounts like that. I wanted to leave a tip for the staff and I assumed I was short changed by mistake. But Tony’s response to a simple inquiry left me very unhappy. You cannot choose to rip off customers and then insult them when you get caught. And then I found out that an older couple from South Africa were also ripped off the same way. So this was a pattern. 

Anyway, I didn’t want to keep the change so I gave it back to them but they kept pushing the note towards me and insisted I keep it. No apology for the mistake or Tony’s little quip. I complained to the tour guide in front of the staff member and told her exactly what happened. Tony and the other staff member kept defending what they did initially. After much discussion, and after I demanded an apology, he said he was sorry. 

I think most Vietnamese people are very pleasant but this was not a good experience. I understand this this restaurant has won awards etc but this was completely undeserving of that sort of recognition. The staff need to be trained to treat all customers regardless of their ethnicity the same way. I didn’t see Tony commenting on the white South African man who was also ripped off and who also demanded his change.

Decent Food, Nice ambience, Uncomfortable Situation
Mar 2019 • Couples
My wife and I dined here. My wife's meal ,which was a fried noodle with beef plate, was well seasoned and she liked it very much. I found the broth in my beef pho soup to be tasty, however, the meat itself was bland in my opinion. The ambience was great and we thought our waiter was very attentive and professional, which we were happy with. Unfortunately, our uncomfortable situation was not with him, but rather the manager. My wife and I like fruit shakes without added sugar. We recognize that some fruits can be simpler in taste than others but we prefer our fruits natural without added refined sugar. The mango shake we ordered came out bitter and very acidic. We have had many mango shakes in our lives, and we know when a mango shake is made with a mango that is ripe and sweet and this was not one of those times. The manager changed our order for a watermelon shake, however, she proceeded to try and explain that she would charge us for the mango shake, which we gave back. We of course refused to pay for the mango shake and that is how the conversation ended. In our opinion, it is important that a restaurant takes more consideration for the ripeness of the fruit they use for their shakes rather than try and cover the unsweeteness of something by adding sugar. It would have been nice not to have encountered this situation. Opinons usually are subjective, and this is ours. We would not return here again, but it doesn't mean that others will not enjoy their time.

Very nice off-street restaurant
Oct 2017 • Friends
We visited The Oasis couple of times as we were staying at Beautiful Saigon Hotel (attached to the restaurant) so we had a chance to try few different types of menu served thru the day. 
The breakfast was rather basic: not so much to choose from hot snacks (or maybe we've missed it) however, lots of fruits and fresh juices. 
The lunch: many tour operators using this place for lunches included in their excursions. The food really depends on the set menu it was chosen for you. More or less fancy. The food in general very good, sometimes I had a feeling some dishes were prepared in a rush to accommodate a higher number of guest. e.g beef and pork were dry and chewy. 
The dinner is a different story. Dishes from the menu card are wonderfully served, delicious, decent size and very well priced. The selection is impressive, covering Vietnamese, Asian, American and European dishes so, no matter how many times you come, you can always try something new. 
The bar offers a wide selection of alcoholic and soft drinks. All similarly priced o other places in this area. Latest menu selection and prices can be found at restaurant website.
The Restaurant is hidden in the small side street, off Bui Vien, offering very pleasant and quiet atmosphere during your meal. The modern décor and very nice outdoor pool are surrounded by plants creating a feeling of an oasis right in the heart of the Saigon’s bustling backpacker area. 
The pool is not very big but it is kept clean and sunbeds are located on a terrace above the pool. There is an entrance fee for non-hotel guests of 100.000 VND (towels incl). If you’re staying at the Beautiful Saigon Hotel then pool for free of charge (no towels provided).
